name: dbx160-parallel-punch
description: Parallel ('New York') dbx 160 on a drum bus: hard RMS limiting (Inf:1, low threshold) blended UNDER the dry. Because the dbx's fully-wet signal is already high-crest/punchy (transients ride over a crushed body) but quiet, the parallel blend mostly restores BODY + level + density while keeping the punch — the dbx parallel is a density/weight move, not a transient-restore move. compress Inf:1, thresh -30, mix 50. VALIDATED on the Watercolors warm drum bus: LUFS -17.18->-16.74 (+0.44 denser at the same -1 dBFS peak), crest 17.17->16.73, low-band RMS -20.1->-19.7 (body filled), LRA 2.44->2.21, true-peak -0.98, centroid 1747->1753 (tone preserved). Weight/density with the transients intact.
intended_for: a drum bus that wants more weight/density + sustained body without losing transient snap
plugin_build: uaudio_dbx_160.vst3 (UADx native build — renders headless & processes offline; the /Components/UAD dbx 160.component + Universal Audio UAD dbx 160 twins PASS THROUGH offline, do not use them).
notes: compress 'Inf:1' and meter/sc_filter are string/bool enums -> apply_vst_preset.py only (apply-vst-chain's float dict can't set them).

mix is the built-in parallel blend (0=dry, 100=fully crushed wet). Unlike an opto comp where the wet is dense/low-crest, the dbx wet is HIGH-crest (RMS-detector signature) -> blending toward dry restores body/level/density, not transients.
Lower thresh = harder wet (more body crushed). Inf:1 at thresh -30 is a firm RMS limiter on the body.
Clean VCA (THD ~0.05% even at Inf:1) -- the density is dynamic, not saturation. dbx 160 = MONO. Hand the result to master-track.
